newsitem.title: UK: BT, News International launch online service.
newsitem.headline: BT, News International launch online service.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc and News International Plc said on Wednesday they planned to launch an Internet service called Springboard, designed for the British mass consumer market.

The service, due to be launched in January 1997, will provide fast and easy access to content drawn from major News International and News Corporation titles, such as The Times, The Sunday Times, The Sun and the News of the World.

"Unlike current services, which appeal only to limited sectors of the community, Springboard will have the depth of material and ease of use to appeal to a wide range of households," said BT multimedia services director Rupert Gavin.
"We will be able to offer teenagers help with their homework as well as news on their favourite football team, while providing parents with the latest in holidays, banking or local events," he added.
As well as enjoying "unique high-quality content", customers would be able to use e-mail, chat online, participate in interactive debates and post their own Internet pages, BT said.

BT said Springboard would work with third party partners to provide a broad spectrum of services including up-to-the-minute local and national news, weather, sport, events, listings and ticketing, as well as games, retailing and a definitive reference library.

"With News International's expertise in publishing, multimedia and news gathering, and BT's experience in multimedia and communications, the new venture will establish a very attractive service for the UK market," said Douglas Flynn, managing director of News International.
BT is rapidly expanding into booming Internet markets.

BT's initiatives include CampusWorld, its on-line education service for schools; BTnet, an internet access service for business customers; BT Internet, its mass market dial Internet service and Wireplay, a computer games network.
